properties.name: WHAT WORKED (field log 2026-10-05, re-measured on the v0.79.0 assets): the release's checksums.txt verified a hand-downloaded tarball (`sha256sum -c --ignore-missing`). The unpacked binary's hash (0d2237cf…) let the reporter prove after the fact that the binary already installed was the release's. Do not regress it
properties.statement:
Field log entry [works] (art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, lines 368-371): "the release checksum flow (`sha256sum -c --ignore-missing checksums.txt`) confirmed the tarball, and the unpacked binary was byte-identical to the one already installed (`0d2237cf…`), so verification after the fact was possible."

RE-MEASURED with v0.79.0's checksums.txt and `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing`: reflow2-kit.tar.gz OK, reflow2-mcp-linux-x86_64.tar.gz OK. The unpacked reflow2-mcp hashes to sha256:0d2237cf5a7b3bcc04eb…, the prefix the reporter recorded. install.sh runs the same check before installing, and refuses on a mismatch. So the flow serves a hand install as well as the installer.
